tiers.name: Find your way
tiers.blurb: The Unity windows and safety nets you use every day.

tiers.name: First recolour
tiers.blurb: Pick a part, change its colour, save a new PNG.

tiers.name: Pieces and paint
tiers.blurb: Keep edits on one area and paint on layers.

tiers.name: Layer craft
tiers.blurb: Mix, clip and shape layers like a painting app.

tiers.name: Shaders and upload
tiers.blurb: How materials, shaders and VRChat treat your texture.

tiers.name: Power tools
tiers.blurb: Import settings, colour space and baked maps.

entries.title: Hierarchy
entries.tip: Lists everything in your scene. Click a part to select it.
entries.definition: The list of everything in your open Unity scene, including your avatar and its parts.
entries.what: Like a family tree for your scene: your avatar is the parent, and its body, hair and clothes are its children.
entries.when: When you want to choose which part of your avatar to edit.
entries.example: Open your avatar's arrow, click Body, then press “Edit this part”. Avistry opens that part's texture to edit.
entries.tryIt: Click any part of your avatar in the Hierarchy, then press “Edit this part”.
entries.watchOut: Check the avatar's name on the button before you press it. A scene can hold several avatars.
entries.whereInUnity: Hierarchy window, usually on the left. Click an entry to select it.

entries.title: Scene view
entries.tip: The 3D window where you see and click your avatar.
entries.definition: Unity's 3D window where you look around your scene and click things in it.
entries.what: Like a photo studio where you can walk around your model. Avistry lets you click or paint on the avatar there.
entries.when: When you want to pick pieces or paint on the avatar itself instead of on the flat texture.
entries.example: Alt+drag turns the camera. Turn on “Click the model to select pieces”, then click a sleeve: that piece is selected.
entries.tryIt: Open the Scene view, turn on “Click the model to select pieces” and click your avatar.
entries.watchOut: While painting on the model, drags paint. Hold Alt to move the camera. Esc stops painting.
entries.whereInUnity: Scene tab, centre. Reopen it from Window > General > Scene.

entries.title: Inspector
entries.tip: Shows the settings of whatever you selected.
entries.definition: The panel that lists every setting of the object, material or file you have selected.
entries.what: Like the spec sheet attached to an item: select a material, texture or avatar part and its settings appear.
entries.when: When Avistry tells you to change a setting in Unity itself, such as an image's import settings.
entries.example: Click an image in the Project window and the Inspector shows its Texture Type, sRGB and compression settings.
entries.tryIt: Open the Inspector, then click your avatar's part in the Hierarchy.
entries.watchOut: The Inspector shows only what is selected now. Clicking another object changes what it shows.
entries.whereInUnity: Inspector window, usually on the right.

entries.title: Project window
entries.tip: Your project's file browser, listing every asset.
entries.definition: The window that shows all the files in your Unity project, in folders.
entries.what: Like the file explorer inside Unity: saved PNGs, materials and saved edits all appear here.
entries.when: When you want to find a file Avistry made, or select an image to check its settings.
entries.example: After “Save as new PNG”, open the folder next to your original texture. The new Hoodie_col_ats.png is there.
entries.tryIt: Open the Project window and find an image under Assets.
entries.watchOut: Files appear under Assets. A file outside Assets, such as one in Downloads, isn't part of the project.
entries.whereInUnity: Project window, bottom. Files live under the Assets folder.

entries.title: Asset
entries.tip: Any file Unity manages, like an image or a material.
entries.definition: A file in your Unity project: an image, a material, a model or a saved edit.
entries.what: Like items in a toolbox: each one is a file in your Assets folder.
entries.when: When Avistry says it made a new file: a PNG, a material copy or a saved edit.
entries.example: Pressing “Save as new PNG” on Hoodie_col makes three new assets: Hoodie_col_ats.png, a material copy and a saved edit.
entries.tryIt: Add a layer, then press “Save edit for later”.
entries.watchOut: Your original texture file is never overwritten. Avistry always writes new assets next to it.
entries.whereInUnity: Project window, Assets folder.

entries.title: Prefab
entries.tip: A saved object that many scenes and avatars can share.
entries.definition: A reusable saved copy of an object. Change the prefab and every copy follows.
entries.what: Like a cookie cutter: change the cutter and every cookie changes.
entries.when: When Avistry warns that a material is shared with other avatars or prefabs.
entries.example: A Hoodie material is used by two avatar prefabs. Updating it changes both avatars, so Avistry offers “Use a copy instead”.
entries.watchOut: The blue cube icon marks a prefab. Treat prefab materials as shared unless you know otherwise.
entries.whereInUnity: Blue cube icon in the Hierarchy and Project window.

entries.title: Undo and redo
entries.tip: Ctrl+Z steps back one action. Ctrl+Y steps forward.
entries.definition: Unity's way to take back your last change, and to bring it back again.
entries.what: Like an eraser for editor actions: it covers most layer, paint, material and save changes in Avistry.
entries.when: When a change isn't what you wanted, or you want to compare before and after.
entries.example: Paint three strokes on a Hoodie layer, then press Ctrl+Z twice. Only the first stroke stays.
entries.tryIt: Make a change in Avistry, then press Ctrl+Z.
entries.watchOut: Changes to an image's import settings can't be undone with Ctrl+Z. Undo them in the Inspector.
entries.whereInUnity: Edit > Undo, or Ctrl+Z. In Advanced, the History list in the Paint tab shows the steps.

entries.title: Simple and Advanced
entries.tip: Simple hides rarely used controls. Nothing is removed.
entries.definition: Simple shows the everyday controls. Advanced shows every setting too.
entries.what: Like a dashboard with a switch that hides the spare dials. Advanced puts them all back.
entries.when: When you want fewer buttons while you learn, or finer control once you know the basics.
entries.example: Press “Simple” at the top right. The Blend menu then lists every blend mode, not only Normal, Multiply and Color.
entries.tryIt: Press “Simple” at the top right of the texture view.
entries.watchOut: Switching never deletes your edits. Advanced settings you changed stay applied even when Simple hides them.
entries.whereInUnity: Not a Unity feature. It is the Simple / Advanced button in Avistry's toolbar.

entries.title: Part
entries.tip: The 3D shape of one part of your avatar, like a jacket.
entries.definition: One separate 3D object of your avatar, such as the body, hair or a jacket.
entries.what: Like one garment on a mannequin. Your avatar is made of several, such as body, hair and clothes.
entries.when: When you choose what to edit. Each part has its own materials and textures.
entries.example: Click Jacket in the Hierarchy, then press “Edit this part”. Only the jacket's textures are listed; the hair keeps its own.
entries.tryIt: Pick a part with “Edit this part” or “Choose a part from a list”.
entries.watchOut: A part can have several materials, and parts can share one. Check the Material and Texture lists.
entries.whereInUnity: Mesh Renderer or Skinned Mesh Renderer component in the Inspector.

entries.title: Renderer
entries.tip: The component that draws a part using its materials.
entries.definition: The component on a part that draws its shape on screen using its materials.
entries.what: Like a projector that shows the sculpture on screen. Avatar parts use a Skinned Mesh Renderer or a Mesh Renderer.
entries.when: When Avistry mentions an empty material slot, or you need to see which materials a part uses.
entries.example: Select Body and open the Inspector. Its Skinned Mesh Renderer lists three Materials: skin, eyes and mouth.
entries.watchOut: A part with an empty material slot can't be edited there. Pick another slot or part.
entries.whereInUnity: Inspector, Skinned Mesh Renderer or Mesh Renderer, Materials list.

entries.title: Material
entries.tip: The asset that says how a part looks.
entries.definition: A file that sets a part's look: which shader it uses and which textures and colours.
entries.what: Like a paint recipe card: it names the paint type and lists the images and colours to use.
entries.when: When a part looks wrong or you want to recolour it. One part can have several materials.
entries.example: Hoodie has two materials, Cloth and Zip. Pick Zip in “Material” to edit its texture instead.
entries.tryIt: Pick another entry in “Material” on a part with several materials.
entries.watchOut: Several parts can share one material. Changing the shared one changes them all.
entries.whereInUnity: Project window (.mat file), or the Materials list on a Renderer.

entries.title: Texture
entries.tip: The flat picture wrapped onto a part.
entries.definition: The flat image that a material wraps around a part to give it colour or detail.
entries.what: Like wrapping paper around a gift: the paper is flat, the gift is 3D.
entries.when: When you want to change how a part looks. You edit the texture, not the shape.
entries.example: Hoodie_col is the hoodie's colour texture. Paint a star on it in “Paint” and the star shows on the hoodie.
entries.tryIt: Choose another image in “Texture”.
entries.watchOut: Avistry edits colour textures. A normal map or mask texture holds data, not colour.
entries.whereInUnity: Select an image in the Project window; its settings appear in the Inspector.

entries.title: Hue
entries.tip: Which colour it is: a spot on the colour wheel.
entries.definition: The colour itself, apart from how light or how strong it is.
entries.what: Like a clock hand pointing at a ring of colours. Turning it moves red to orange to yellow.
entries.when: When a part already has colour and you want a new one with the same shading and highlights.
entries.example: Red hair: drag “Colour shift (hue)” until it turns green. The darker strands stay darker, so the shading is kept.
entries.tryIt: Move “Colour shift (hue)” on any part and let go.
entries.watchOut: White, grey and black have no hue. Use “Cover with one colour” on them instead.
entries.whereInUnity: Unity colour pickers show hue as H when set to HSV.

entries.title: Tint
entries.tip: Covers a colour with one colour and keeps the shading.
entries.definition: Giving a part one new colour while its light and shadow stay as they were.
entries.what: Like holding coloured cellophane over a picture: the light parts show the full colour, the dark parts stay dark.
entries.when: When the part is white or grey, where changing the hue does nothing.
entries.example: White jacket: choose “Cover with one colour”, pick pink and set Strength to 80%. The folds stay shaded.
entries.tryIt: Switch “Which part” to One piece at a time, click a part, then press “Cover with one colour”.
entries.watchOut: Very dark parts stay dark under a tint. Use “Brightness” to lift them.
entries.whereInUnity: Main Color property on many materials.

entries.title: Save
entries.tip: Writes your layers into a new image file.
entries.definition: Combining all your layers into one new image, with a copy of the material that uses it.
entries.what: Like flattening a layered drawing into one printed sheet. Afterwards the layers are part of the picture.
entries.when: When you are happy with the result and want it to show on your avatar and upload.
entries.example: On Hoodie_col, press “Save as new PNG”. You get Hoodie_col_ats.png and a new material for the hoodie; the original stays.
entries.tryIt: Add a layer, then press “Save as new PNG” and confirm.
entries.watchOut: Save empties your layer list, because the edit now lives in the new image. Ctrl+Z brings it back.
entries.whereInUnity: Save tab, then the Project window.

entries.title: PNG
entries.tip: A lossless image format that keeps transparency.
entries.definition: The image file type Avistry saves. It keeps every pixel exactly and supports see-through areas.
entries.what: Like a photo printed without blur. JPG softens detail and can't be see-through.
entries.when: When you save: Avistry always writes a new PNG, so your original image is never replaced.
entries.example: Saving Hoodie_col writes Hoodie_col_ats.png next to it. Press “Show file” to jump to the new file.
entries.tryIt: Save an edit, then press “Show file”.
entries.watchOut: A JPG source has already lost detail. Saving as a PNG stops it getting worse.
entries.whereInUnity: Imports as a Texture2D in the Project window.

entries.title: UV map
entries.tip: Says where each spot on the flat image lands on the model.
entries.definition: The guide that matches every spot on the flat texture to a spot on the 3D shape.
entries.what: Like the cutting pattern for a garment: it says which flat piece becomes which part of the 3D shape.
entries.when: When you want to pick pieces or paint on the avatar. Both need the part to have a UV map.
entries.example: Open View › UV wireframe above the texture. The thin lines outline the pieces of the Hoodie map.
entries.tryIt: Turn on UV wireframe in the View menu, then click a piece on the texture.
entries.watchOut: A part with no UV map can't be picked by piece or painted on. Choose another part.
entries.whereInUnity: Not editable in Unity. It is made in Blender or another modelling app. Avistry draws it as UV wireframe.

entries.title: Piece
entries.tip: One connected shape on the texture sheet, like one sleeve.
entries.definition: A connected shape on the flat texture that wraps one area of your avatar.
entries.what: Like one pattern piece in a sewing pattern: a sleeve, a collar or a front panel.
entries.when: When a colour or a brush stroke must stay on one area and not spill onto its neighbours.
entries.example: Hoodie: select both sleeve pieces in “Limit”, then brush across the whole hoodie. Paint appears only on the sleeves.
entries.tryIt: Turn on “Click the model to select pieces”, then click one piece of your avatar.
entries.watchOut: Left and right often share one piece of texture, so both sleeves change together.
entries.whereInUnity: Unity has no piece view. Blender and other modelling apps call them UV islands.

entries.title: Seam
entries.tip: Where two texture pieces meet on the model.
entries.definition: The line on the model where two separate texture pieces join.
entries.what: Like the stitching between two fabric pieces: a flat brush stops at the edge of each piece.
entries.when: When a stroke on the avatar crosses from one piece onto another and shows a break.
entries.example: Paint across the hoodie's side seam with “Smooth across joins” off and the line breaks. Turn it on and the line continues.
entries.tryIt: Turn on “Paint directly on the model (Scene view)”, then “Smooth across joins”, and paint across a join.
entries.watchOut: Smooth joins work with round brush tips. Smudge and scattered tips still stop at seams.
entries.whereInUnity: Visible as sharp breaks in paint on the model. Seams are set in Blender, not Unity.

entries.title: Layer
entries.tip: One edit on a see-through sheet above the texture.
entries.definition: A single change, such as paint or a colour adjustment, kept on its own sheet above the texture.
entries.what: Like clear plastic sheets stacked on a drawing: the top sheet covers the ones below.
entries.when: When you want to hide, reorder or delete one change later without touching the rest.
entries.example: On Hoodie_col, add a Paint layer and draw a star. Click the eye beside the layer and the star disappears; nothing else changes.
entries.tryIt: Paint a stroke on your avatar's texture. Avistry adds a Paint layer for it.
entries.watchOut: The top layer is in front. If paint vanishes, check the layer's eye icon and opacity.
entries.whereInUnity: Not a Unity feature. Layers live in Avistry's Paint tab.

entries.title: Opacity
entries.tip: How solid something is. 0% is invisible.
entries.definition: How solid a layer or brush stroke is: 100% is solid, 0% is invisible.
entries.what: Like frosted glass: the lower the opacity, the more of the layers underneath shows through.
entries.when: When paint looks too strong, or seems to have vanished. Check opacity first.
entries.example: On a pink Paint layer, drag “Layer opacity” to 40%. The pink turns soft and the hoodie shows through.
entries.tryIt: Select a layer and drag “Layer opacity”.
entries.watchOut: “Paint strength” and “Layer opacity” are two different dials. Paint vanishes if either is at 0%.
entries.whereInUnity: Sliders in Avistry. Unity colour pickers call it Alpha.

entries.title: Blend mode
entries.tip: How this layer mixes with the layers beneath it.
entries.definition: The rule that decides how a layer's colours combine with the colours under it.
entries.what: Like mixing paint on a palette: cover it (Normal), darken it (Multiply) or tint it (Color).
entries.when: When paint should shade or recolour what is below instead of covering it.
entries.example: Make a grey layer, set “Blend” to Multiply and paint under the hoodie's arms. They darken but keep their detail.
entries.tryIt: Change “Blend” on a layer and let go.
entries.watchOut: Simple mode lists Normal, Multiply and Color. Switch to Advanced for all the others.
entries.whereInUnity: Not a Unity feature. It is the Blend menu in a layer's settings in Avistry.

entries.title: Mask
entries.tip: Black and white image: white shows the effect, black hides it.
entries.definition: A black and white picture that decides where a layer or a shader effect shows.
entries.what: Like masking tape on a wall: taped areas stay clear of paint, open areas get it.
entries.when: When only some areas should change, such as the eyes glowing or only the hem shining.
entries.example: On a Paint layer open “Limit this layer”, press Add mask › Hide everything, then paint Show over the sleeves.
entries.tryIt: Open “Limit this layer” on a layer and press Add mask.
entries.watchOut: Hiding with a mask deletes nothing. Paint with Show over the same area to bring the layer back.
entries.whereInUnity: Effect masks are textures in the Material Inspector. Layer masks exist only in Avistry.

entries.title: Clipping
entries.tip: The layer shows only where the layer below has paint.
entries.definition: A layer only shows where the layer directly below it shows.
entries.what: Like colouring inside an outline: shading stays inside the base shape.
entries.when: When shadows or highlights must stay on the base colour and never spill over its edges.
entries.example: Clip a grey Multiply layer to the skin layer with “Clip to layer below”. The shading stays on the arm and skips the sleeve.
entries.tryIt: Select a layer above another and tick “Clip to layer below”.
entries.watchOut: The bottom layer can't be clipped, and a hidden base layer hides the clipped layer too.
entries.whereInUnity: Not a Unity feature. It is a tick box in a layer's settings in Avistry.

entries.title: Gradient map
entries.tip: Recolours by brightness and keeps the shading.
entries.definition: A layer that gives each pixel a colour from a gradient bar, based on how bright it is.
entries.what: Like tinted film over a black and white photo: the shading stays and only the colours change.
entries.when: When you want a whole new colour scheme for hair or cloth and still keep its shading.
entries.example: Brown hair: press “Change colours”, then change the bar from dark brown to light blonde. The strands keep their shine.
entries.tryIt: Press “Change colours” in the empty layer list, or add Gradient Map in Advanced.
entries.watchOut: Black areas always take the bar's first colour and white areas its last, whatever the original colours were.
entries.whereInUnity: Not a Unity feature. It is a layer type in Avistry.

entries.title: Channels
entries.tip: The red, green, blue and see-through parts of a pixel.
entries.definition: The four numbers stored for every pixel: red, green, blue and alpha.
entries.what: Like four stacked transparencies, each with its own picture. Together they make the colour you see.
entries.when: When a mask texture packs several effects into one image and you must change only one.
entries.example: A packed mask has glow in its green channel. Turn off R, B and A in “Channels” to paint only the glow.
entries.tryIt: Select a layer and toggle R, G, B or A in “Channels”.
entries.watchOut: With all four channels off a layer does nothing. Press Turn all on to fix it.
entries.whereInUnity: Texture Inspector channel buttons (R G B A).

entries.title: Alpha
entries.tip: The see-through part of a pixel. 0 is clear.
entries.definition: The fourth channel of an image: how solid each pixel is, from fully clear to fully solid.
entries.what: Like the clear part of a sticker's backing: where alpha is 0 you see through to what is behind.
entries.when: When part of an image, such as lace or hair strands, must be see-through.
entries.example: Press Erase and rub over a stroke on a Paint layer. That stroke goes clear again and the texture below shows.
entries.tryIt: Choose Erase in “Paint tools” and rub over a stroke on a Paint layer.
entries.watchOut: A see-through texture still looks solid until the material's rendering mode is Cutout or Transparent.
entries.whereInUnity: Texture Inspector, Alpha Is Transparency.

entries.title: Ambient occlusion
entries.tip: Darkens creases where light cannot reach.
entries.definition: Soft shading in folds and gaps where parts are close together, measured from your model.
entries.what: Like the dark line where a book meets a shelf. It is measured from the model's current pose.
entries.when: When flat colours need depth, such as under the hair, at collars and between fingers.
entries.example: Press “Bake ambient occlusion” on the Hoodie. A Multiply layer called Ambient occlusion appears; lower its Layer opacity for lighter shading.
entries.tryIt: Press “Bake ambient occlusion” on a colour texture.
entries.watchOut: Shading follows the model's current pose. A relaxed T-pose gives the most even result.
entries.whereInUnity: Not a Unity setting. Avistry bakes it in Make maps (Advanced).

entries.title: Shader
entries.tip: The program that decides colour, light and shine.
entries.definition: The program a material uses to draw a surface: its colour, light, shadow and shine.
entries.what: Like the type of paint: matte, glossy or metallic. The material picks one and fills in its settings.
entries.when: When a material looks pink, flat or wrong, or you can't change its colours.
entries.example: The hoodie turns pink in the Scene view: press “Check materials”. It lists the broken material and offers a fix button.
entries.tryIt: Press “Check materials” to scan every material on your avatar.
entries.watchOut: Nothing changes until you press a fix button. Image fixes can't be undone with Ctrl+Z.
entries.whereInUnity: Material Inspector, Shader menu at the top.

entries.title: Locked shader
entries.tip: A frozen Poiyomi shader. Unlock it to change colours.
entries.definition: A Poiyomi material that has been optimised and frozen, so its settings no longer change.
entries.what: Like laminating a document: faster and smaller, but you can't write on it any more.
entries.when: When Recolour says a material is locked. Unlock it first; Poiyomi locks it again at upload.
entries.example: Hair uses a locked Poiyomi material. Press “Unlock”, then drag “Colour shift (hue)”: the hair changes colour.
entries.tryIt: Press “Unlock” when a locked material shows it.
entries.watchOut: If upload says Unlocked Shaders were found, lock the materials again in their Poiyomi Inspector.
entries.whereInUnity: Material Inspector, Poiyomi Lock / Unlock button.

entries.title: Poiyomi
entries.tip: A popular VRChat avatar shader with many effects.
entries.definition: A widely used avatar shader for VRChat with extras such as glow, rim light and matcaps.
entries.what: Like a premium paint range with extras. Avistry finds its colour settings and recolours them for you.
entries.when: When your material's shader name shows Poiyomi. Recolour edits it; a locked one needs unlocking first.
entries.example: A hair material shows Poiyomi Toon in its Shader menu. Open “Recolour” and “Colour shift (hue)” changes its colour settings.
entries.tryIt: Pick a part whose material uses a Poiyomi shader.
entries.watchOut: Locked Poiyomi materials ignore colour edits until you unlock them. “Unlock” does it.
entries.whereInUnity: Material Inspector shows Poiyomi in the shader name.

entries.title: lilToon
entries.tip: An anime-style VRChat shader. Recolour supports it.
entries.definition: A popular toon shader for anime-style VRChat avatars, with soft shadows and outlines.
entries.what: Like a premium paint range tuned for anime looks: flat colour bands, soft shadows and clean outlines.
entries.when: When your material's shader name shows lilToon. Recolour and Face shadow both work with it.
entries.example: A hair material shows lilToon. Drag “Colour shift (hue)” in “Recolour”: its shadow, rim and outline colours follow along.
entries.tryIt: Pick a part whose material uses a lilToon shader.
entries.watchOut: Its rendering mode (Opaque, Cutout, Transparent) sets whether see-through areas show. Avistry warns when they disagree.
entries.whereInUnity: Material Inspector shows lilToon in the shader name.

entries.title: Render queue
entries.tip: The draw order and see-through type of a material.
entries.definition: A material setting that decides when it is drawn and whether see-through areas show.
entries.what: Like deciding which sheets go on the table first: opaque things go down first, see-through ones later.
entries.when: When see-through areas such as lace or lashes look solid, or a solid material is set to Transparent.
entries.example: A lashes texture has see-through edges but shows as a solid block: set the material to Cutout and the edges clear.
entries.watchOut: Transparent costs more to draw than Opaque or Cutout. Use it only where you need soft see-through edges.
entries.whereInUnity: Material Inspector: Rendering Mode (lilToon) or Rendering Preset (Poiyomi), and Render Queue.

entries.title: VRChat upload
entries.tip: Publishing your avatar with the VRChat SDK.
entries.definition: Sending your finished avatar to VRChat through the SDK's Control Panel.
entries.what: Like sending your finished costume to the venue: only the files your avatar really uses go with it.
entries.when: When you are ready to publish. Check shaders and textures first, because an upload is slow to repeat.
entries.example: Before upload, run “Check materials” on the hoodie. It flags broken materials and Crunch-compressed images you can fix first.
entries.watchOut: Avistry adds nothing to your avatar at upload. Only your saved PNGs and material copies go up.
entries.whereInUnity: VRChat SDK menu › Show Control Panel › Builder.

entries.title: Import settings
entries.tip: How Unity reads an image: colour mode, size, compression.
entries.definition: The per-image settings that tell Unity how to read, size and compress an image file.
entries.what: Like printer settings for one file: they change how every material using it looks, not the picture itself.
entries.when: When Avistry shows an image warning, or colours look washed out, blocky or blurry.
entries.example: Hoodie_col looks washed out and Avistry says sRGB is off. Press “Fix import setting” and the colours come back.
entries.tryIt: When an image warning shows, press “Fix import setting”.
entries.watchOut: Import fixes change the image file's settings, so every material using it changes. Ctrl+Z can't undo them.
entries.whereInUnity: Texture Inspector, after you select the image in the Project window.

entries.title: sRGB colour space
entries.tip: Whether Unity reads an image as colour or raw data.
entries.definition: A setting that tells Unity if an image's numbers are colours or plain data values.
entries.what: Like reading a thermometer in Celsius or Fahrenheit: the same number means different things.
entries.when: When colours look washed out, or a mask or normal map behaves oddly.
entries.example: Hoodie_col was imported with sRGB off, so it looks pale. Avistry offers “Fix import setting”, which switches sRGB on.
entries.watchOut: Colour images need sRGB on. Masks and normal maps need it off. Avistry flags a mismatch.
entries.whereInUnity: Texture Inspector, sRGB (Color Texture).

entries.title: Mipmap
entries.tip: Smaller copies of a texture, used when it is far away.
entries.definition: Ready-made smaller versions of a texture that Unity uses as the camera moves away.
entries.what: Like carrying a postcard of a poster: from far away the small copy looks the same and weighs less.
entries.when: When a texture shimmers or looks too soft at a distance, check its mipmap filter.
entries.example: Hair looks fuzzy from across the room. In Advanced, Avistry says the mipmap filter is Box; press “Fix import setting” to use Kaiser.
entries.watchOut: Turning mipmaps off makes distant textures sparkle. Leave them on for avatars.
entries.whereInUnity: Texture Inspector › Advanced › Generate Mip Maps and Mip Map Filtering.

entries.title: Seam padding
entries.tip: Fills the gap around pieces so no line shows.
entries.definition: Spreading each piece's edge colours outward into the empty texture space around it.
entries.what: Like extra paint around a card's cut edge: the colour carries a little way past each piece's border.
entries.when: When thin light lines appear along seams from a distance. Avistry adds this padding itself when you save.
entries.example: Hoodie_col saved at 2048 px: each piece's edge colours spread about 16 pixels outward, so no pale line shows.
entries.watchOut: Pieces that sit closer than the padding can mix edge colours slightly. Avistry warns you after the save.
entries.whereInUnity: Not a Unity setting. Avistry applies it when it saves a colour texture.

entries.title: Normal map
entries.tip: Fakes bumps and lighting. It holds data, not colour.
entries.definition: A texture that stores the direction of tiny surface bumps, so lighting looks detailed without extra shape.
entries.what: Like braille on a flat sheet: your eyes read light and shade from it, not colour.
entries.when: When a flat part needs stitches, scales or fabric grain that catch the light.
entries.example: On Hoodie_col press “Make normal map”: stitches become bumps in Hoodie_col_normal.png. Press Apply to material to see them.
entries.tryIt: Press “Make normal map” on a colour texture.
entries.watchOut: Never paint colour onto a normal map: it breaks the lighting. Edit the colour texture instead.
entries.whereInUnity: Texture Inspector, Texture Type: Normal map.

entries.title: Face shadow map
entries.tip: A texture that makes toon face shadows sweep cleanly.
entries.definition: A smooth map that tells a toon shader which parts of a face are shaded at each light angle.
entries.what: Like a stencil for the face: as the light turns, it decides exactly which areas fall into shade.
entries.when: When an anime face shows blotchy shadows from the nose or eyes. Use it on the face part only.
entries.example: On the face part of a lilToon avatar, press “Make face shadow map”, then Apply to material. The shadow now sweeps across smoothly.
entries.tryIt: Pick your face part, then press “Make face shadow map”.
entries.watchOut: If the shadow lands on the wrong side, tick “Swap left and right” and make the map again.
entries.whereInUnity: lilToon: Shadow › Mask type SDF. Poiyomi: Shading › Lighting type SDF.

entries.title: AI helper (MCP)
entries.tip: An optional way to let your AI app do the busy work.
entries.definition: An AI app on your computer that works in Avistry for you, through MCP for Unity.
entries.what: Like asking an assistant to hold the brush while you watch. Every move is its own Ctrl+Z step.
entries.when: When you can describe the job in words, like recolouring both sleeves pastel pink.
entries.example: Ask your AI app: make the hoodie sleeves pastel pink. It selects the sleeve pieces and adds a recolour layer you can undo with Ctrl+Z.
entries.tryIt: Set up an AI helper, ask it to save a PNG, then click Allow.
entries.watchOut: Names of parts, materials and textures go to your AI service. Pictures go only if you click Allow.
entries.whereInUnity: Not a Unity feature. It needs the separate MCP for Unity package; the AI helper window explains the steps.
